event.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 28?
event.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 28 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data is unavailable or missing for the observation period, Weather Underground will be used as the secondary resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Market-implied odds strongly favor a highest temperature of 25°C or higher in London on August 28, 2026, backed by real-time observations showing afternoon peaks near or above this threshold.** Southwesterly flow advected milder maritime air across southern England, supporting daytime maxima around 22–25°C under partly cloudy skies with limited precipitation. Official Met Office and station data from Heathrow recorded values climbing to approximately 25°C midday, consistent with late-summer climatology where August highs frequently reach the mid-20s when blocking patterns or warm advection dominate. Traders' near-certain consensus reflects verified station readings and short-range model agreement rather than speculation. A realistic challenge would require rapid post-peak cooling, localized measurement discrepancies between urban and airport sites, or revised official verification placing the daily maximum below 25°C, though current data make such outcomes unlikely.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) and multiple meteorological services project a daytime maximum of 31–33°C for Tokyo on August 28, 2026, with 32°C as the central expectation.** This aligns closely with the market-implied odds showing near-certainty for exactly 32°C, reflecting trader assessment of real-time data rather than speculation.

Persistent cloud cover, scattered showers, and northeasterly flow have moderated temperatures throughout the day, consistent with climatological August averages near 31°C and recent observations peaking in the low-to-mid 30s°C. Model consensus and JMA guidance issued on August 27 emphasized these conditions, limiting upside potential beyond the forecast range. 

Traders assign negligible probability to outliers (under 1% combined) because any significant deviation would require rapid changes in steering patterns or insolation not supported by current observations or ensemble runs. The primary risk to the 32°C resolution remains minor timing or measurement variance in official station data, though the strong consensus across agencies supports the current positioning.
